rows.summary: This guide demonstrates how to access the Kubernetes API from within a Pod, including using official client libraries, directly accessing the REST API, and using kubectl proxy.

topics: Pod creation with ServiceAccount token projection
rows.summary: This guide explains how to configure ServiceAccounts for Pods in Kubernetes, including using the default service account, opting out of API credential automounting, using multiple ServiceAccounts, and manually creating API tokens.
This document explains how to extend the Service IP range assigned to a cluster, allowing for more available IPs for Services.
This document provides a step-by-step guide to migrate from PodSecurityPolicy to the built-in PodSecurity Admission Controller in Kubernetes, focusing on minimizing risks and ensuring security.

This document provides good practices and considerations for designing admission webhooks in Kubernetes, including the importance of good webhook design, identifying whether admission webhooks are used, choosing an admission control mechanism, and more.

Dynamic volume provisioning allows storage volumes to be created on-demand, eliminating the need for manual provisioning calls to cloud or storage providers. It enables cluster administrators to define multiple storage flavors with custom parameters, allowing end users to select from various storage options without worrying about the underlying provisioning complexities.

This document provides an overview of the different approaches to managing Kubernetes objects using the kubectl command-line tool, including imperative commands, imperative object configuration, and declarative object configuration.
This document provides guidance on hardening the Kubernetes scheduler configuration to improve security posture, including authentication, authorization, and networking settings.
Provides information on how Kubernetes implements and controls API access, including authentication methods, admission controllers, authorization mechanisms, and service accounts.
A CustomResourceDefinition is a Kubernetes API object that allows you to extend the built-in API for your environment by defining new custom resources.

This document outlines the minimum kernel version requirements for various Kubernetes features and sysctls, emphasizing the importance of kernel compatibility for different operating system distributions.
A probe is a check performed by the kubelet against a running container in a pod to determine the container's state and health, influencing its lifecycle.
This document explains how to define and apply admission policies in Kubernetes, including validating and mutating admission policies, their API types, policy elements, CEL expressions, and actions.
This tutorial guides you through deploying a sample application to minikube, including running the app and viewing application logs.
